title: Design a Recommendation System
interviewAnswer: Clarify candidate generation, ranking objective, feedback signals, cold start, popularity bias and top-k evaluation. Often use a two-stage architecture: fast candidate retrieval followed by richer ranking.
why: Recommender design questions combine candidate generation, ranking, feedback, bias, latency and business constraints.
intuition: First narrow millions of possibilities to a manageable candidate set, then rank candidates with richer features, then apply business/safety constraints.
deepDive: Clarify users/items/relevance and online latency. Offline path builds interaction/features/embeddings and trains candidate/ranking models. Online path fetches user/query context, generates candidates, ranks, filters unavailable/ineligible items and returns top-K. Handle cold start with content/popularity/rules. Evaluate Recall@K/nDCG offline and user/business outcomes online; account for exposure bias and feedback loops.
workedExample: A content platform can retrieve a few thousand candidates using collaborative/content embeddings, rank them with richer user-item-context features, apply eligibility/diversity constraints and return the top-K results.
commonMistakes: Designing only one giant scoring model without candidate generation.
Treating missing interactions as true dislikes.
Ignoring availability/workload or popularity feedback loops.
followUps: How do you handle cold start?
How do you avoid popularity bias?
production: Log impressions, rankings and outcomes; refresh features/graph, monitor concentration and latency, and retain rule-based fallback candidates if the model is unavailable.
